calls.exactPrompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: HD reinterpretation of WATER_SPE resource 36 / item 0 / picture 0, one complete opaque logical 64 by 64 animation picture. Produce one original high-resolution square PNG, preferably 1280 by 1280; preserve the entire composition, not a sprite sheet.
Reference roles: Image 1 is the exact original native picture 0 and is PRIMARY authority for the complete silhouette, pose, placement, occlusion and water shapes. Image 2 is the exact same packed bits freshly decoded as large diagnostic cells and is PRIMARY readable geometry; do not paint the pixel grid. Image 3 is an accepted HD historical game frame for painting finish, restrained natural lighting and existing muted armor materials ONLY. Do not copy its stone walls, rocks, character pose or scenery.
Task: transform the native black-and-white water picture into detailed, restrained hand-painted historical Three Kingdoms game art. Faithfully follow the broad curling water crest across the upper band, the sweeping diagonal white water shapes and the smaller curling currents across the lower half. Interpret them as natural turbulent river water and foam, with subdued gray-green water and pale foam, without colored magic. The one small partly submerged helmeted human figure has its dark rounded head mass around the native center-left; its bent, occluded body and limbs follow the native diagonal shapes toward the lower right. Preserve the exact native picture 0 positions, size and occlusions. The person's head and upper body must remain small within the complete water scene. Where native detail is ambiguous, use restrained material shading inside the existing silhouette rather than inventing a new object or weapon. Do not enlarge the person into a portrait or invent uncovered feet.
Composition and finish: complete square picture edge to edge, same narrow dark areas at the top and edges as the native picture. The entire frame, including gaps, is opaque. Natural charcoal-green shadow areas, muted weathered bronze/dark historical helmet and clothing only where the native silhouette supports them; same realistic brush texture and soft light as Image 3, while preserving the water scene's geometry. No added landscape, horizon, boats, horses, troops, flags, buildings, stones or new props. No giant wave at a new position. The native frame's readable shape governs the result.
Constraints: original opaque PNG, NO alpha transparency. No text, digits, damage numbers, UI, labels, watermark, border, colored glyphs, electric effects, effect trails or literal black-and-white pixel pattern. One complete native picture 0 reinterpreted in HD, with a single partially concealed figure and the supplied native water shapes.

observations.native: Picture0 has the large head/person silhouette left of centre around the middle height; picture1 places the head/person farther right with a different narrower surrounding visible silhouette. Native pixel evidence does not establish a named weapon or person identity.
observations.hd: Picture0 has one bronze-helmeted head left of centre; picture1 has the corresponding one-person head right of centre. Body/shoulders are partly submerged/hidden by waves. Broad frame positions and two distinct poses are retained; not claimed as exact pixel registration.

observations.native: Both frames have upper broad curling water bands/checkered crests and strong lower diagonal strips descending toward the right; the two lower patterns and person contours differ.
observations.hd: Both images keep curling upper foam/waves and several lower right-down diagonal surges. Water fills the opaque square. The two frames have visibly different water/person arrangements.

observations.observation: Exactly one visible human in each candidate, chiefly head/upper shoulders; waves obscure the lower body. No added soldiers, boats, coastline, magic symbols or independent weapon.
No visible text, numbers, interface panels, logos, frames or narrative props. Helmet and visible armor use the accepted character material treatment rather than adding a named lord identity.
Actual visual inspection confirms two different frames, rather than relying on different file hashes alone.

Compared actual accepted Stone42 picture0: charcoal-green tone, restrained bronze helmet/armor and realistic hand-painted detail continue into the water candidates. Stone rubble/rod props are absent from WATER.

limits: Art acceptance concerns the original static images only. Native movie cadence/live clears, displayed NUM15 damage, input lifecycle and final compositing remain separate actual runtime gates.
Generated detail interprets the small bitmap; no claim that every native pixel, hand anatomy or unidentified feature is literally reproduced.

acceptance.runtime: See docs/validation/m4-water-20261009.json for separately recorded actual player casts and native label/NUM15/hold validation. Static art acceptance alone proves no gameplay; the first LCD route failed before any cast.
